sources.note: Classification Erap > Finungwan-Mamaa-Gusan; alternate name Nema; only reference shown is Hooley & McElhanon 1970. No descriptive source listed.
Stub; cites Ethnologue 18th ed. and Retsema, Potter & Gray 2009 (SIL Electronic Survey Report 2009-015) for the name Nema. No phonology.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority (submitted by Chris Rice, SIL-PNG). 2015. Change Request 2015-039: add name 'Nema' for [gsn].
sources.note: Name-change request only: speakers in Kokosan, Gom, Damet, Finongan call the language Nema; cites Retsema, Potter & Gray 2009 (SIL ESR 2009-015). No phonology.

sources.citation: McElhanon, Kenneth A. 1984. A linguistic field guide to the Morobe Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-57.
sources.note: Village list only: (64) Gusan pop. 869, villages Boiran, Borin, Gom, Gusan, Nandalamen. No phonology, no stress.

sources.citation: Claassen, Oren R. & Kenneth A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Finisterre Range - New Guinea. Papers in New Guinea Linguistics 11 (Pacific Linguistics A-23), 45-78. Canberra: ANU.
sources.note: Gusan entry (2.7.3, p. 56) is a one-paragraph lexicostatistical/survey note (pop. 800, some dialectal variation). Section 6.1 gives phonological sketches of Rawa, Suroi, Wantoat, Uri, Uruwa languages etc., not Gusan. The only stress remark (p. 66) reads: "Stress is phonemic in Rawa but probably sub-phonemic in Yupna and Wantoat. In none of these languages does it carry a heavy functional load." Nothing on Gusan stress.

sources.citation: Hooley, Bruce A. & Kenneth A. McElhanon. 1970. Languages of the Morobe District - New Guinea. In Wurm & Laycock (eds), Pacific Linguistic Studies in Honour of Arthur Capell (Pacific Linguistics C-13), 1065-1094.
sources.note: Lexicostatistical survey only (Gusan 35% with Nimi, 40% with Irumu, 30% with Sakam; pop. 800, village list). No phonology, no stress.
56 lexical items, all from McElhanon & Voorhoeve (1970/1973) comparative wordlist; no phonological description.
